group_assessment.weighting: A single-centre retrospective chart review of infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) in a tertiary programme that adopted first-line vigabatrin plus prednisolone. The observation (association of symptomatic VABAM with simultaneous hormonal therapy) is firm within its design; the authors themselves refuse the causal reading and name disease severity as an alternative. No WWOX patient is identified.

entries.proposition: Eleven of the 17 VABAM cases were symptomatic, in a cohort of 108 vigabatrin-treated children.
entries.snippet: Overall, we identified 17 children with VABAM, of which 11 were symptomatic (sVABAM) and 6 were asymptomatic (aVABAM).

entries.proposition: All 11 symptomatic VABAM cases had simultaneous hormonal therapy, against 40 of 91 without identified VABAM.
entries.snippet: All 11 children with sVABAM were treated with VBG‐HT, in comparison to 40 of 91 children without identified VABAM (p = 0.001).

entries.proposition: Peak vigabatrin dose was not associated with any VABAM category, contrary to the group's earlier cohort.
entries.snippet: peak vigabatrin dosage was not associated with aVABAM, sVABAM, or any VABAM (all p >> 0.05, Table 1 and Figure 1B)

entries.proposition: Table 1: simultaneous hormonal therapy and vigabatrin by VABAM class.
entries.snippet: Simultaneous hormonal therapy and vigabatrin, n (%) | 40 (44%) | 15 (88%) | 0.001 | 4 (67%) | 0.41 | 11 (100%) | 0.001

entries.proposition: Of the asymptomatic cases, hormonal exposure did not differ, in an underpowered comparison.
entries.snippet: concomitant hormonal therapy was observed in 4 (67%) children with aVABAM and 17 (44%) children without VABAM, with p = 0.40

entries.proposition: Genetic etiologies, including CDKL5 deficiency, are among the symptomatic cases; no gene-level association is tested.
entries.snippet: In the two patients with CDKL5 and unknown etiology, the timing of symptom onset and offset was closely related to VGB‐HT exposure.

entries.proposition: The authors state that causation is not established and name disease burden as a rival explanation.
entries.snippet: it is possible that our identified associations of VABAM with vigabatrin dosage (prior study) or concomitant hormonal therapy (prior and current study) are proxies for a link between VABAM and disease burden

entries.proposition: Design limits: retrospective, non-uniform MRI, non-random treatment, radiologist not blinded to exposure.
entries.snippet: Radiologist's clinical impressions, on which our identification of VABAM was based, were not blinded to vigabatrin exposure.

entries.proposition: No mechanism of harm is identified.
entries.snippet: the absence of an identified mechanism of harm

entries.proposition: The authors judge VABAM risk small against the risk of continued spasms.
entries.snippet: the risk and consequences of VABAM are small relative to the risk of continued epileptic spasms
